tasks.short: Protect confidential information throughout translation and interpreting work.

steps.what: Review the brief, confidentiality terms and permitted recipients.
Exercise discretion about information heard, seen and shared during the assignment.
Resolve unclear permission or disclosure requests with the responsible information owner.
File assignment records and remove working copies under the retention policy.

tasks.design: Configure an assignment checklist, restricted folders and retention rules in the {DOCS}, linked to assignment correspondence in the {EMAIL}. Show approved handling requirements before work starts and route unusual disclosure requests to the information owner; discretion during conversations stays with the interpreter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Confidentiality depends on context and personal conduct. Administrative controls often stop at separate folders, agreements and mailbox habits.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing access and retention settings can cover routine handling. Small integrations are easier to build, but no model is needed for the proposed controls.
tasks.still_hard: Off-platform copies, oral disclosures and conflicting instructions remain difficult. GDPR and applicable national rules shape access, retention and any employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an apparently harmless detail that would expose a person, negotiation or commercial plan.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into checking agreements and tidying files. The person retains discretion during assignments; no new disclosure rights are assumed.

reach.task: Prepare a confidential briefing for an external spokesperson.
reach.learn: Embargo handling, recipient verification and the boundary between authorised briefing and disclosure.

evidence.claim: Access restrictions, retention configuration and handling checklists can support confidentiality without replacing professional judgement.
Marketing translation has no general exemption from GDPR obligations.

assumptions: This describes handling work attributable to assignments, not the full duration of confidential conversations.
Shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Retention automation uses an approved schedule, respects holds and covers supported repositories.
No conversation recording or employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which confidentiality terms and retention schedules apply?
Who can authorise disclosure and resolve conflicting instructions?
Which repositories and mailbox controls are available?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which handling failures arise from missing controls, and which arise from ambiguous authority?
Can existing configuration cover the relevant records without custom integration?
new_work: Maintain handling categories and retention rules.
Resolve access exceptions and conflicting disclosure requests.
Check that supported repositories apply the approved controls.
tasks.statement: Follow ethical codes that protect the confidentiality of information.

tasks.short: Resolve conflicts in meaning, cultural interpretation and intended wording.

steps.what: Identify conflicting interpretations in source wording or stakeholder feedback.
Gather cultural context and compare plausible wording options.

loop.input: Conflicting interpretations, audience brief and retrieved cultural or terminology evidence.
loop.output: Alternative wordings, supported implications and questions for stakeholders.
loop.check: Require traceable evidence for factual claims; translator checks cultural assumptions and removes unsupported assertions.
loop.stop: At most three options and one revision; unresolved cultural claims go to a qualified reviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can organise options but cannot draft contextual alternatives from conflicting free-text interpretations.

steps.what: Discuss intended meaning and cultural consequences with the marketing manager.
Approve the intended claim and wording after translator advice.
Update the translation and record the agreed meaning and rationale.

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} evidence and a bounded drafting loop to prepare wording options before a human discussion. Record approval of the exact wording through {WORKFLOW}, then apply that approved text and its rationale to the specified document version in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conflicts depended on tacit intent and cultural context. Preparing options and preserving decisions required separate manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can assemble evidence-backed options, while deterministic version checks and approvals handle the resulting paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Offence, humour, gesture and implied promises depend on audience and situation. Stakeholders may disagree about intent, and live interpretation leaves little time for preparation.
tasks.human_edge: The translator notices discomfort, asks tactful questions and explains cultural consequences without taking ownership of another person's intended message.

ambition.what: Cultural meaning review before campaign concept approval

tasks.altitude: More time goes to early discussions of culturally sensitive concepts and less to rebuilding context. The translator advises on linguistic risk; the marketing manager retains the decision on the intended claim.

reach.task: Review campaign wording for audience interpretation and reputational consequences.
reach.learn: Stakeholder mapping, issue escalation and message approval.

evidence.claim: Evidence-backed option drafting and human cultural mediation are proposed workflow choices.
The digest documents invented AI quotations, supporting source verification rather than trust in fluent output.

assumptions: The steps describe written marketing conflicts with time for stakeholder discussion.
Live oral or sign-language conflict resolution remains a human activity; preparation and decision records can still improve.
Automatic document updates insert only exact approved wording into a matching version; version conflicts stop the update.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; confidential context uses authorised processing.
Employee consultation follows national rules where applicable and is included in access planning.
unknowns: What proportion of conflicts arises during live interpretation?
Who has authority to approve claims and culturally sensitive wording?
Which language communities require external specialist review?
Can the document store support stable passage identifiers and version checks?
research_questions: Do prepared options help stakeholders resolve meaning conflicts sooner?
Which cultural assertions are insufficiently supported by available references?
What escalation criteria distinguish linguistic uncertainty from disputed business intent?
new_work: Check drafted options for stereotypes and unsupported cultural claims.
Maintain escalation contacts for difficult language and audience questions.
Handle document version conflicts after approval.
Review whether recorded decisions remain suitable when audience or campaign context changes.
tasks.statement: Identify and resolve conflicts related to the meanings of words, concepts, practices, or behaviors.

tasks.short: Interpret spoken or signed messages while preserving meaning, context and style.

steps.what: Review the assignment brief, participants and approved terminology.
Agree interpreting mode, turn-taking, visibility and clarification signals with participants.
Deliver simultaneous or consecutive interpretation through speech or signs.
Pause for clarification or correct an interpretation when meaning is uncertain.

tasks.design: Generate a compact interpretation brief from structured assignment details and approved glossary entries in the {DOCS}, using the {CALENDAR} for session details. The interpreter reviews the brief, agrees session arrangements and delivers the live interpretation, including clarification and correction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Live interpretation requires low latency, contextual judgement and immediate repair. Preparation is often assembled separately for each assignment.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic templates and document links can remove repeated briefing assembly. The proposed change requires no advance in automated speech or sign interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Irony, overlapping speech, dialect, cultural references and sign-language variation remain demanding. Preparation savings do not create additional live interpreting capacity automatically.
tasks.human_edge: Preserving intent while managing pace, dignity, uncertainty and relationships in real time.
tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter and more consistent, while most assignment time remains live interpreting. No new language competence or decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Design an accessible multilingual session run sheet.
reach.learn: Interpreter scheduling, sightlines, audio routing, speaker pacing and participant access needs.

evidence.claim: Structured assignment data and approved terminology can populate a briefing template deterministically.
Glossary software supports preferred terminology across language pairs; this does not establish live interpreting quality.
The digest provides no documented case establishing reliable autonomous spoken or sign-language interpretation for these assignments.

assumptions: The baseline is a scheduled marketing meeting or event; remote delivery changes the channel.
The preparation generator selects approved material without translating or inventing content.
Listening and meaning preparation are detailed in task 9335 and must not be added again as separate assignment hours.
Shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which languages, sign languages and interpreting modes are required?
How much assignment time currently goes into preparation?
Are assignment briefs and approved glossaries consistently available?
What access arrangements do participants require?
research_questions: Which briefing fields prevent the most avoidable interruptions?
Can interpreters retrieve the generated brief quickly in their actual working environment?
new_work: Maintain briefing templates and glossary links.
Check participant details and missing preparation material.
Review whether generated briefs omit essential context.
tasks.statement: Translate messages simultaneously or consecutively into specified languages, orally or by using hand signs, maintaining message content, context, and style as much as possible.

tasks.short: Proofread, edit and revise translated materials before release.

steps.what: Retrieve the translation draft, source text and applicable language guidance.
Check spelling, terminology and formatting in the translation editor in {OTHER}.
Compare source and translation for meaning, omissions, tone and audience fit.

loop.input: Aligned source and target segments, language check results, term base and style guide.
loop.output: Proposed findings with source references and severity.
loop.check: Check segment references mechanically; translator assesses findings and checks unflagged passages.
loop.stop: One pass per segment and one retry for malformed output; uncertain passages return to the translator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect term mismatches but cannot reliably judge implied meaning, register or cultural fit.

steps.what: Revise wording and accept the final translated text.

loop.input: Translation draft, source text and translator-accepted findings.
loop.check: Rerun terminology and integrity checks; translator accepts edits and approves the complete text.
loop.stop: One revision pass and one repair pass; unresolved wording is edited manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Context-sensitive revisions require language generation beyond fixed replacements.

steps.what: Send the approved version and record its review status.

tasks.design: Configure the translation editor in {OTHER} to load versioned material from {DOCS} and run terminology, spelling and integrity checks. A bounded bilingual review loop proposes findings and tracked revisions; the translator approves the text before {WORKFLOW} records and routes the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Language checks already existed, but contextual comparison required sustained bilingual reading. File versions and review records were often disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language comparison can supplement existing checks. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting files, checks and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle omissions, persuasive wording and specialised claims still need expert review. Confidential material requires GDPR-compliant processing and appropriate EU AI Act transparency where applicable.
tasks.human_edge: The translator recognises when technically correct wording changes intent, credibility or cultural meaning.

ambition.what: Pre-publication language-risk review for multilingual campaign variants

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward disputed meaning, sensitive claims and release decisions. The translator retains language approval; campaign publication rights remain with the editor.

reach.task: Review multilingual campaign copy before publication.
reach.learn: Editorial risk assessment, claim substantiation and publication approval criteria.

evidence.claim: Terminology enforcement is available in existing translation software.
Existing software checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and style.
A vendor-reported case describes fewer translation edits after introducing language-quality controls.
Bilingual model review still requires translator validation; the proposed remaining-time shares are estimates.

assumptions: The translation editor in {OTHER} supports bilingual files or segment exports.
Most material is editable text; complex layouts remain exceptions.
Time shares and build ranges describe a narrow pilot, not measured customer performance.
Access estimates include employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Available file interfaces and existing language-check capabilities.
Language pairs, terminology coverage and specialist subject matter.
Required independence of the final reviewer.
Permitted processing environments and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which serious errors does the bounded review miss in a representative bilingual sample?
Do false alarms consume more review time than they save?
new_work: Review proposed findings and check samples of unflagged text.
Maintain term bases, style rules and evaluation examples.
Resolve failed imports, broken alignment and version conflicts.
Review access controls and processing arrangements.
tasks.statement: Proofread, edit, and revise translated materials.

tasks.short: Check technical terminology for accuracy and consistency across translation revisions.

steps.what: Compare current and previous translations in the {OTHER} translation workbench.
Check changed technical terms against the approved term list and earlier occurrences.
Read flagged passages to distinguish errors from justified contextual variations.

loop.input: Flagged term occurrences, aligned source passages, term definitions and audience constraints.
loop.output: Suggested error or justified variation, with evidence and an optional tracked correction.
loop.check: Validate term references and segment identifiers; translator checks meaning and every proposed correction.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per flagged segment; missing definitions remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: String rules detect inconsistency but cannot determine whether a different sense requires different wording.

steps.what: Accept corrections and approve justified terminology exceptions.
Save check results and terminology decisions with the revised translation.

tasks.design: Configure revision comparison and terminology checks in the {OTHER} translation workbench using versioned approved terms. A bounded loop proposes explanations and tracked corrections for contextual exceptions; accepted changes and check results are saved to {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Term lists and revision histories were not always connected. Simple matching also produced false alarms for valid contextual variation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing terminology checks handle much of the task. Smaller custom connectors and bounded exception classification reduce the remaining manual comparison work.
tasks.still_hard: Inflection, compound words, ambiguous source terms and inconsistent source copy create false positives. Shared terminology changes can affect many approved assets.
tasks.human_edge: The translator distinguishes consistent wording from consistent meaning and accepts exceptions when the context requires them.

ambition.what: Terminology change impact alerts for published marketing assets

tasks.altitude: The translator reviews meaningful exceptions and advises editors about assets affected by term changes. They gain a proposed right to recommend terminology migrations; content owners still approve publication changes.

reach.task: Assess which published assets require revision after terminology changes.
reach.learn: Publication inventories, revision ownership and release scheduling.

evidence.claim: DeepL glossaries support preferred terminology; they do not establish that every contextual exception can be resolved automatically.
Acrolinx supports repeatable style-guide checks and quality gates.
The digest reports a Roche vendor case with 30% fewer translation edits; this is not a forecast for this workflow.

assumptions: The translation workbench retains source and target segments and revision history.
Approved terms have language, concept and version identifiers.
Checks operate on content rather than individual employee performance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; access planning includes consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Does the translation workbench already provide configurable terminology checks?
Are source and translation versions reliably aligned?
Who approves shared term-list changes?
How many contextual exceptions occur in the main language pairs?
research_questions: Can configuration alone achieve an acceptable exception rate?
How much additional error detection does contextual classification provide?
Which language-specific morphology rules reduce false alarms?
new_work: Review proposed corrections and contextual exceptions.
Maintain term versions, exclusions and language-specific rules.
Investigate failed segment alignment and missing revisions.
Check that new term rules do not damage previously valid translations.
tasks.statement: Check translations of technical terms and terminology to ensure that they are accurate and remain consistent throughout translation revisions.

tasks.short: Translate written source material into specified languages while preserving meaning and document structure.

steps.what: Confirm target language, audience, purpose, deadline and required review.
Read the source and identify ambiguous passages, claims and specialist concepts.

loop.input: Source text and translation brief, divided into referenced sections.
loop.output: Proposed ambiguities, specialist terms and questions for the source owner.
loop.check: Require source references; translator reads the source and confirms issues without treating silence as clearance.
loop.stop: One analysis pass and one schema repair; unresolved meaning goes to the source owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Term lists cannot identify all contextual ambiguities or implicit references.

steps.what: Find approved terms and reusable segments in the translation editor in {OTHER}.
Translate passages and resolve wording against the source and brief.

loop.input: Source segments, surrounding context, resolved source issues, approved matches and terminology.
loop.output: Aligned translated segments with unresolved choices flagged.
loop.check: Check segment coverage, numbers, names and placeholders; translator post-edits meaning and specialist wording.
loop.stop: One generation pass and one repair per segment; unresolved or sensitive passages return to manual translation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Approved matches cover repeated wording; novel passages require contextual language generation.

steps.what: Restore document structure and check tables, links and text placement.
Hand the draft and unresolved questions to the language reviewer.

tasks.design: Capture the brief in {WORKFLOW}, retrieve approved matches from the translation editor in {OTHER}, and preserve source structure from {DOCS}. Bounded loops flag source ambiguities and draft unmatched segments; deterministic checks validate integrity before translator post-editing and routing to the separate proofreading and approval task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Translation memory helped repeated text, but novel material still required extensive drafting and research. File handling and source clarification remained separate activities.
tasks.enabler_now: Contextual machine translation can handle unmatched passages while existing terminology controls constrain output. AI-assisted coding makes document handling and review routing cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: Legal and scientific meaning, scanned documents and low-resource language pairs remain difficult. GDPR, confidentiality, rights to source material and applicable EU AI Act duties constrain processing and release.
tasks.human_edge: The translator resolves ambiguity with the source owner and judges whether a fluent translation preserves the intended claim.

ambition.what: Minority-language customer groups previously excluded from campaign briefings

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from first drafts to source clarification, post-editing and specialist review. The translator can recommend language coverage, while budget and publication decisions remain with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Improve source documents before multilingual publication.
reach.learn: Controlled language, source ambiguity reduction and structured document authoring.

evidence.claim: Existing translation software supports glossary-based terminology enforcement.
A commissioned composite reports substantial translation productivity gains; it does not establish this customer's savings.
Translation memory, structural checks and translator post-editing form a practical deterministic-first workflow.

assumptions: Most sources are editable documents with stable segment identifiers.
Approved memories and terms exist for at least the main language pairs.
This task ends at a reviewable draft; final proofreading and language approval belong to the connected task.
Build estimates cover a small set of file types and language pairs.
Access ranges include consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Actual language pairs, volumes and document formats.
Quality and reuse rights of existing translation memories.
Which documents require specialist, certified or independent translation.
Approved processing locations, retention periods and contractual restrictions.
research_questions: Which language pairs meet the required meaning-preservation standard after post-editing?
Which document formats lose structure during extraction and reconstruction?
How much review remains for legal and scientific passages?
new_work: Resolve source ambiguities before drafting.
Review machine translations and failed integrity checks.
Maintain approved memories, terms and document adapters.
Evaluate quality separately by language pair and subject.
Handle restricted documents through an approved manual route.
tasks.statement: Read written materials, such as legal documents, scientific works, or news reports, and rewrite material into specified languages.

tasks.short: Consult reference sources to choose accurate translations for uncertain terms.

steps.what: Identify terms whose meaning is uncertain in the source passage.
Search the {OTHER} translation workbench for approved terms and previous translations.
Compare specialist references, definitions and usage examples against the passage.

loop.input: Uncertain passage and retrieved excerpts from approved reference sources.
loop.output: Candidate meanings with quoted evidence, source locations and unresolved differences.
loop.check: Verify quotations and source locations mechanically; translator checks relevance and conflicting definitions.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass across at most six excerpts; return unresolved questions to translator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact lookup retrieves terms but cannot compare competing senses across free-text definitions.

steps.what: Choose the contextual meaning and record the supported translation.

tasks.design: Configure approved-term and translation-memory lookup in the {OTHER} translation workbench, with reference files indexed from {DOCS}. A bounded comparison loop drafts cited alternatives only when lookup leaves ambiguity; the translator selects the meaning and records the decision in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference material was scattered, differently formatted and difficult to search together. Contextual meaning still required specialist reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing terminology lookup handles known terms. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting reference stores, while bounded text comparison can prepare evidence for unresolved senses.
tasks.still_hard: Rare language pairs, outdated references, licensed dictionaries and specialist meanings remain difficult. A fluent explanation can still support the wrong sense.
tasks.human_edge: The translator recognises when an apparently correct term misrepresents the intended claim or audience context.

ambition.what: Cited terminology guidance for campaign writers

tasks.altitude: The translator spends less time searching and more time resolving difficult meanings. They can curate reusable guidance for writers; approval of technical claims stays with the subject specialist.

reach.task: Maintain controlled vocabulary for product documentation.
reach.learn: Concept definitions, source authority and terminology versioning.

evidence.claim: DeepL glossaries support consistent preferred terminology; this supports the lookup component, not contextual correctness.
A governed reference search with a bounded comparison loop is a proposed design, not a documented deployment in this digest.

assumptions: Typical work includes written marketing translation and reference preparation for interpretation.
A translation workbench may be internal or provided through a language-service partner.
Reference retrieval respects licences and document permissions.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; translation has no general journalistic exemption.

tasks.statement: Refer to reference materials, such as dictionaries, lexicons, encyclopedias, and computerized terminology banks, as needed to ensure translation accuracy.

tasks.short: Compile and approve bilingual terminology with context and source references.

steps.what: Collect source documents, earlier translations and existing glossary entries.
Extract candidate terms and record provisional equivalents in a working term list.

loop.input: Approved source passages, aligned prior translations and existing glossary entries.
loop.output: Candidate terms, provisional equivalents, context, source spans and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Validate source spans and language tags; preserve approved matches; reject unsupported equivalents and flag conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document batch; failed or unsupported entries enter manual research.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matching reuses known terms but misses new multiword concepts and context-dependent equivalents in prose.

steps.what: Check candidate meanings, equivalents and usage against reliable reference material.
Resolve uncertain technical meanings with a subject specialist.
Approve preferred terms, alternatives and restrictions for the target audience.
Update the translation workbench term base and distribute the approved glossary.

tasks.design: Connect approved material in the {DOCS} to the translation workbench and term base in the {OTHER}, using deterministic matching and deduplication first. A bounded extraction loop proposes new terms with source context in a review queue in the {WORKFLOW}; the translator checks meaning and approves changes before deterministic synchronisation. Generate versioned glossary packs from approved entries for campaign contributors.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source material, prior translations and specialist explanations are scattered. Term extraction requires reading prose, while maintaining connectors and a usable review queue has taken disproportionate effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing term bases handle approved matches. Bounded extraction can propose unfamiliar terms, and AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the surrounding imports, validation and review screens.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible equivalent may be wrong for a legal, medical or product context. Specialist availability, reference rights, confidential content and inconsistent source terminology still constrain progress.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the correct concept and audience-appropriate equivalent, especially when authoritative sources disagree.

ambition.what: Versioned bilingual terminology packs for external campaign writers.

tasks.altitude: The translator spends less time collecting and copying terms and more time settling disputed concepts with specialists. They can offer terminology packs and recommend preferred wording; authority over regulated claims remains with the responsible specialist.

reach.task: Apply approved multilingual terminology across campaign copy.
reach.learn: Editorial style rules, permitted variants and how terminology changes affect existing content.

reach.task: Maintain a concept-based product glossary.
reach.learn: Concept definitions, source authority and distinctions between product versions.

evidence.claim: Glossary software can enforce preferred terminology across language pairs.
A vendor case reports 30% fewer translation edits after terminology and style support; this is not a forecast for this design.
Deterministic term matching can be combined with bounded extraction and translator approval.
The proposed build ranges and remaining-time estimates require customer validation.

tasks.short: Adapt translated learning materials to students’ comprehension levels with educational staff.

steps.what: Discuss learning objectives and comprehension needs with educational staff.
Agree vocabulary, explanation depth and suitable examples with educational staff.
Draft an adapted translation in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Source material, approved adaptation criteria and term base; exclude unnecessary student details.
loop.output: Adapted translation draft with source references and marked explanatory additions.
loop.check: Check required terms, numbers and omissions; translator checks meaning and educational suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved meaning or suitability returns to the translator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates and terminology rules cannot rewrite explanations while preserving meaning across languages.

steps.what: Review meaning and educational suitability, then correct the draft in {DOCS}.
Obtain educational approval and send the adapted material through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An intake form in {WORKFLOW} stores adaptation criteria and links source material in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop applies the term base and marks explanatory additions; the translator checks fidelity and the educational lead approves delivery through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comprehension needs were discussed informally, and suitable wording required language and educational judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured briefs, reusable term bases and bounded drafting reduce preparation effort. AI coding makes the small intake and checking tools cheaper to build.

tasks.short: Listen to speakers, determine meaning and prepare interpretation cues.

steps.what: Retrieve relevant terminology and background material before listening.
Check headphones, listening channels and audibility with the event technician.
Listen for meaning, tone, references and uncertainty in the speaker's statements.
Record concise cues for sequence, names, figures and intended meaning when needed.

tasks.short: Check that translations preserve meaning, content and tone, consulting authors when needed.

steps.what: Retrieve matching source and translation versions from {DOCS}.
Compare content, meaning and tone, recording discrepancies in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Aligned source and translation passages, translation brief and approved terminology.
loop.output: Candidate omissions, additions and shifts in meaning or tone, with both passages cited.
loop.check: Validate passage references and mechanical checks; translator reads the complete text and judges findings.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per section; uncertain findings stay unresolved for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch numbers and terms, but cannot reliably assess implication, register or emotional tone.

steps.what: Send focused questions about ambiguous passages through {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Translator-selected ambiguous passages and unresolved fidelity findings.
loop.output: A short question draft containing exact source quotations and alternative interpretations.
loop.check: Verify quotations against the source; translator checks necessity, wording and recipient before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per question set; translator writes questions that remain unclear.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each ambiguity needs a specific explanation that a fixed question template cannot provide.

steps.what: Discuss intended meaning and tone with the author.
Revise the translation and record fidelity approval in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Version links in {DOCS} assemble a review pack, while deterministic checks compare terms, numbers and missing sections. A bounded comparison loop proposes cited fidelity findings and question drafts; the translator controls author contact and records approval in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files were difficult to align, and semantic checking depended on close reading and author knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Version controls and text alignment handle preparation. Bounded comparison can highlight possible meaning shifts for a translator to assess.
tasks.still_hard: Irony, ambiguity, cultural references and deliberate departures remain difficult. A model may miss a fluent but wrong translation.
tasks.human_edge: The translator understands intent, negotiates ambiguity with the author and accepts responsibility for the final wording.

ambition.what: Resolve translation-impacting ambiguity before each campaign copy revision is approved.

tasks.altitude: The translator spends less time assembling files and drafting queries, with more time for difficult passages. They gain a structured way to request clarification; editorial publication rights remain with the editor.

reach.task: Identify source-copy ambiguities before multilingual publication.
reach.learn: Editorial intent, tone decisions and version approval practices.

evidence.claim: Terminology enforcement supports consistency checking, but does not prove semantic fidelity.
Style-guide scoring can support repeatable checks alongside human review.
Semantic comparison and author-question drafting are proposed bounded uses; complete human reading remains necessary.

assumptions: Authors or responsible editors are available for material ambiguities.
Approved source and translation versions can be linked.
Share and remaining-time percentages are estimates, not measured savings.
EU GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; employee consultation follows national rules where required.

Which languages and content types require specialist review.
Whether client contracts restrict model processing.

Which finding categories create useful queries rather than extra review?

Monitor changes to model behaviour and document access.
tasks.statement: Check original texts or confer with authors to ensure that translations retain the content, meaning, and feeling of the original material.

tasks.short: Compile source context and audience information into a usable translation brief.

steps.what: Collect the request, source links and audience instructions from the marketing manager.
Read campaign materials and compile product, channel and audience context.

loop.input: Request fields and authorised campaign documents linked to the translation request.
loop.output: Structured brief with source-linked audience, purpose, channel, tone, constraints and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source links; translator checks extracted facts and inferred audience assumptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass over the request packet; absent or conflicting facts become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: A form captures new instructions, but existing campaign documents contain relevant context in varied free-text formats.

steps.what: Identify missing context and prepare questions about audience and intended use.
Clarify audience, tone and unresolved constraints with the marketing manager.
Confirm the compiled brief as the basis for translation.

tasks.design: Configure a request form in {WORKFLOW} that collects source links, language, audience and channel, and stores a versioned brief in {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop fills draft fields from authorised campaign material; deterministic completeness checks prepare questions, and the marketing manager confirms the clarified brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Context arrived across attachments, campaign documents and conversations. Standard forms helped, but could not assemble relevant facts already buried in source material.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and approvals handle intake. Bounded extraction and cheaper custom connectors make source-linked draft briefs practical without replacing the clarification conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may not know the intended audience precisely. Contradictory campaign goals and missing market context cannot be resolved by extraction.
tasks.human_edge: The translator asks questions that expose unstated assumptions about audience knowledge, tone and acceptable adaptation.

ambition.what: Locale-specific audience briefs for market-entry campaigns

tasks.altitude: The translator spends less time assembling background and more time shaping useful audience constraints before translation starts. They can return incomplete requests for clarification; the marketing manager approves audience and campaign intent.

reach.task: Summarise audience evidence for a new market.
reach.learn: Research limitations, audience segmentation and separation of evidence from assumptions.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, completeness rules and versioned approvals can use conventional workflow configuration.
Source-linked context extraction is a proposed bounded model use; the digest provides no direct translation-brief deployment case.

assumptions: Typical requests arrive through a mailbox with links or attachments; some companies already use structured intake.
Audience facts must be sourced or confirmed, rather than invented from the target language.
Completeness rules generate template questions; the translator adds contextual questions during review.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; access and retention follow the sensitivity of campaign material.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; consultation can extend calendar lead time.
unknowns: Is translation intake already structured?
Where are audience research and campaign materials stored?
Who can confirm audience assumptions and intended use?
Which request fields are needed for oral and sign-language interpretation assignments?
research_questions: Which missing brief fields most often cause translation rework?
How reliably can source-linked extraction distinguish stated facts from audience assumptions?
Which requests need a conversation even when all required fields are complete?
new_work: Review extracted context and confirm unsupported assumptions.
Maintain brief templates and completeness rules by content type.
Resolve inaccessible source links and conflicting document versions.
Update briefs when campaign intent or audience changes.
tasks.statement: Compile information on content and context of information to be translated and on intended audience.

tasks.short: Agree translation requirements, delivery terms and any fees with the requester.

steps.what: Review the request and ask for missing files or basic details.
Discuss audience, languages, purpose, terminology, accessibility, deadlines and quality expectations.
Inspect source files in translation software and assess volume, reuse and formatting effort.
Calculate effort and any fee using rates, minimum charges and delivery constraints.
Resolve tradeoffs and negotiate scope, timing and any fee with the requester.
Prepare the written scope, delivery terms, exclusions and any quotation.
Check the scope confirmation and send it to the requester.
Record the requester's acceptance and release the agreed brief for scheduling.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake and acceptance in the {WORKFLOW}, with source files held in the {DOCS} and accepted briefs passed to the {PROJECT}. A deterministic service reads analysis exports from translation software in {OTHER}, applies approved rates and generates scope confirmations from templates. The translator handles discovery and negotiation, reviews exceptions and approves each outgoing confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive with incomplete briefs, file analysis sits apart from pricing, and negotiated terms require repeated entry. These links were possible before but often too small to justify bespoke integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, approval flows and document templates cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building file-analysis adapters and pricing rules; no model loop is required here.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous source text, creative adaptation, inaccessible files and uncertain revision rounds still need judgement. Confidential files require GDPR-compliant handling; EU AI Act duties depend on any AI introduced. National rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The translator uncovers what the requester actually needs, explains quality and deadline tradeoffs, and negotiates commitments they can deliver.

ambition.what: Pre-campaign language readiness review for marketing managers before source copy is final.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less intake chasing and quotation assembly, with more time for difficult briefs and early campaign advice. No new pricing authority follows automatically; delegated fee limits still apply.

reach.task: Plan language coverage and delivery dates for a campaign.
reach.learn: Campaign milestones, audience priorities and how language choices affect launch scope.

reach.task: Prepare source copy for translation.
reach.learn: Source clarity checks, terminology control and revision freeze practices.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, rate calculations, template generation and acceptance routing can use deterministic software.
Discovery and negotiation depend on audience context, quality expectations and commercial judgement.
DeepL provides glossaries for preferred terminology; agreeing terminology requirements is a concrete scoping input.

assumptions: The typical case is written marketing translation; live interpreting requires a different effort model.
An internal translator serves marketing requesters and occasionally handles chargeable work.
Translation software provides file analysis and translation-memory matches; a spreadsheet combines these with rates.
Estimates cover a small implementation using existing platforms and exclude waiting time for consultation or procurement.
Remaining-time percentages are design estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether fees are external charges, internal allocations or absent.
Available translation-software exports and integration permissions.
Approved rates, discount authority and contractual approval limits.
Frequency of scanned files, creative adaptation and live interpreting requests.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Which missing brief fields cause the most follow-up conversations?
How accurately do existing file analyses predict actual effort?
Can requesters accept a versioned scope through a structured approval instead of email?
Which pricing exceptions must reach a translation lead or budget owner?
new_work: Review flagged file-analysis and pricing exceptions.
Maintain rate cards, quote templates and intake fields.
Check that accepted scopes match the versions scheduled for delivery.
Maintain integration access, retention settings and failure alerts.
tasks.statement: Discuss translation requirements with clients and determine any fees to be charged for services provided.

tasks.short: Localize software interfaces and technical documentation for another language and culture.

steps.what: Gather changed strings from localization tools in {OTHER} and technical documents from {DOCS}.
Translate interface strings using translation memory in localization tools in {OTHER}.

loop.input: Unmatched strings, interface context, approved terms and matching translation-memory entries.
loop.output: Localized string draft with unchanged keys and placeholders.
loop.check: Validate keys, placeholders, plural structures and length limits; translator checks meaning in context.
loop.stop: Reuse approved exact matches first; allow one draft and one repair per unmatched batch, then escalate.
loop.why_not_simpler: Memory and rules handle known strings; new wording still requires translation.

steps.what: Translate technical explanations and examples in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Changed technical sections, approved terminology, interface labels and source examples.
loop.output: Localized document draft preserving structure and marking proposed cultural adaptations.
loop.check: Compare commands, warnings, numbers and links; translator checks technical meaning and adaptations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved technical meaning goes to the technical writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact reuse handles unchanged sections; new explanations need language and context-sensitive drafting.

steps.what: Check terminology, placeholders and formatting across localized files in localization tools in {OTHER}.
Review cultural fit and usability in software preview tools in {OTHER}.
Approve the localization pack and hand it to engineering through {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: An integration on {DATA_PLATFORM} collects changed strings from localization tools in {OTHER} and documents from {DOCS}. Approved translation-memory matches are reused, bounded loops draft unmatched content, and deterministic checks validate structure. The translator reviews software previews before an approved pack reaches engineering through {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: String exports, document versions and interface context were disconnected. Custom checks and preview connections were costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing localization features handle reuse and validation. AI coding reduces the effort needed for file adapters and preview connections, with bounded translation for new content.
tasks.still_hard: Short strings lack context, and cultural fit requires judgement. Complex plural forms, right-to-left layouts and technical warnings need careful testing.
tasks.human_edge: The translator recognises misleading interface wording, unsuitable cultural references and changes that affect task completion.

ambition.what: A localized interface preview accompanying each proposed market launch.

tasks.altitude: The translator moves from repetitive string handling toward context review and launch preparation. They can recommend wording and layout changes; engineering retains deployment authority.

reach.task: Review localized layouts and interaction wording before release.
reach.learn: Responsive layouts, bidirectional text, interface constraints and usability testing.

reach.task: Keep interface labels and instructions consistent across releases.
reach.learn: Technical source structure, reusable sections and release versioning.

evidence.claim: Glossaries support consistent preferred terminology across translation work.
A vendor case reports 30% fewer translation edits after terminology and style improvements.
A commissioned composite reports faster translation; its results are not a forecast for this implementation.
Translation memory, file validation and human in-context review can form a deterministic-first localization workflow.

assumptions: The translator supports customer-facing software or digital services alongside marketing.
{OTHER} denotes localization tools and software preview tools.
Approved exact matches are reused only when context and source versions remain compatible.
Build ranges cover one software product and a limited initial language set.
EU GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; consultation follows national rules where required.

Quality and ownership of the translation memory.

Review unmatched strings and culturally sensitive examples.
Maintain adapters, format rules and preview connections.
Investigate failed checks and source changes after translation.

tasks.short: Explain educational interpreters’ responsibilities and working practices to students, families and educational staff.

steps.what: Discuss audience questions and access needs with the educational coordinator.
Prepare role explanations and examples from approved materials in {DOCS}.
Explain responsibilities, confidentiality and classroom working arrangements to participants.
Answer questions and resolve misconceptions about the interpreter’s role.
Send the role guide, agreed arrangements and follow-up responsibilities through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Approved audience-specific templates in {DOCS} generate briefing materials from a structured plan in {WORKFLOW}. The interpreter leads the briefing and questions, then approves a template-based follow-up through {EMAIL} using recorded arrangements and assignments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were recreated for each audience, while useful answers and arrangements stayed in personal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable approved modules and structured follow-up records need configuration rather than a model. Small forms and template connections are cheaper to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, misconceptions and differences in communication access need live explanation. Templates require educational and local-policy review.
tasks.human_edge: The interpreter models effective communication, recognises discomfort and establishes workable boundaries with families and staff.

ambition.what: New family members joining an existing educational support arrangement.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and follow-up take less time, leaving room for additional orientation sessions. The interpreter gains no new authority over educational decisions or support eligibility.

reach.task: Develop clear audience-specific explanations of a professional service.
reach.learn: Audience concerns, accessible messaging and facilitation.

reach.task: Arrange accessible briefings for mixed participant groups.
reach.learn: Access requirements, participant coordination and session logistics.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, structured records and configured delivery can reduce recurring briefing administration.
Live explanations and questions remain human work; no digest case establishes savings for this educational task.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to an educational-services employer or a company working with educational partners.
The company has 200 to 2,000 staff; educational briefings are not typical of every marketing department.
Approved role guidance exists and can be assembled into audience-specific modules.
Follow-up uses interpreter-entered facts rather than meeting recording or automatic transcription.
EU GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; employee consultation requirements vary under national rules.

Who approves role guidance and working arrangements.
Audience languages and communication access needs.
Which participant information may be stored or emailed.

Which formats help families understand roles before attending a live session?

Check follow-up recipients and recorded arrangements.
Assign and close unanswered questions.

tasks.short: Train translators and interpreters, supervise practice and decide readiness for assignments.

steps.what: Select work samples and identify learning needs.
Prepare exercises, examples and feedback notes.

loop.input: Approved examples, explicit training goals and an exercise template.
loop.output: Exercises, proposed answer explanations and coaching prompts.
loop.check: Lead translator verifies answers, difficulty, relevance and removal of identifying details.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; unsupported explanations are replaced manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise exercises but cannot explain contextual language choices for varied examples.

steps.what: Coach through practice, observe performance and discuss alternatives.
Decide readiness, supervision level and the next learning goal.
Record the agreed plan and arrange follow-up practice.

tasks.design: Use {WORKFLOW} to assemble permitted examples from {DOCS} against explicit training goals, with a bounded loop drafting exercises. The lead translator approves the pack, conducts coaching and decides readiness; {WORKFLOW} records the agreed plan and schedules follow-up in {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful examples were scattered, and preparing tailored exercises took time. Coaching and readiness decisions depend on direct observation and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow features can organise examples and follow-up. Bounded drafting reduces exercise preparation without requiring automated employee assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching interpreting involves timing, composure, ethics and interpersonal trust. GDPR, EU AI Act requirements where applicable, and national rules constrain employee-data use and consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor notices hesitation, builds confidence and distinguishes a training need from an unsuitable assignment.

ambition.what: Supervised language practice for marketing staff handling routine multilingual enquiries

tasks.altitude: Preparation and follow-up shrink, leaving more time for observation and individual coaching. Readiness and supervision decisions remain with the lead translator; no new employment decision rights arise.

reach.task: Prepare staff to handle routine multilingual campaign enquiries.
reach.learn: Campaign escalation rules, learning objectives and the limits of staff language competence.

evidence.claim: Templates and configured workflows can organise training examples, records and appointments.
Bounded drafting can assist exercise preparation, but this digest provides no direct translator-training case.
Direct coaching and assignment-readiness decisions remain human work in this design.

assumptions: The role includes supervision of a small internal or contracted language team.
Examples are selected using explicit learning goals, without automated employee ranking.
Existing records can hold an agreed learning plan without a new personnel application.
Build ranges include access review and employee consultation under national rules where required.

Whether work samples may be reused for training.

tasks.short: Accompany and guide tourists in another language, adapting explanations and handling practical needs.

steps.what: Confirm the itinerary, language, meeting point and visitor requirements.
Prepare destination facts, terminology, route notes and visitor explanations.

loop.input: Approved itinerary, verified destination facts, terminology and necessary visitor requirements.
loop.output: Referenced multilingual explanations and practical briefing notes.
loop.check: Guide checks factual references, wording and suitability; itinerary fields must match the approved version.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported facts are removed and difficult wording is prepared manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill logistics, but adapting explanations across languages and audiences requires contextual drafting.

steps.what: Welcome visitors, confirm practical needs and explain the day's arrangements.
Accompany visitors, interpret exchanges and explain destinations in their language.
Decide practical adjustments when conditions or visitor needs change.
Report completion, unresolved requests and useful changes for future visits.

tasks.design: Use {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR} to collect itinerary details, with approved destination material held in {DOCS}. A bounded loop prepares multilingual notes for guide approval, while the guide conducts the visit and makes situational decisions; a short completion form routes follow-up requests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation was spread across correspondence and destination documents. Most task time is physical accompaniment and live interaction, which software cannot remove.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms simplify logistics, and bounded drafting can adapt verified notes into another language. These improve preparation without assuming autonomous guiding.
tasks.still_hard: Live interpretation, accessibility, group dynamics and unexpected conditions require presence and judgement. Visitor requirements can contain sensitive personal data, so GDPR minimisation and appropriate access are necessary; applicable EU AI Act duties depend on the deployed features.
tasks.human_edge: The guide reads the group, builds rapport, interprets local interactions and responds to immediate practical needs.

ambition.what: Small language groups previously unable to book an appropriately prepared guided visit

tasks.altitude: The guide spends less time assembling notes and writing reports, while most of the working day remains with visitors. Operational decision rights remain within existing itinerary and escalation limits.

reach.task: Prepare accessible multilingual visitor itineraries.
reach.learn: Accessibility planning, supplier coordination and contingency arrangements.

evidence.claim: Configured forms, templates and calendar workflows can reduce itinerary administration.
Glossary controls can support consistent terminology in multilingual preparation materials.
The digest provides no direct case establishing automation of live tourist accompaniment.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to an employer offering tourist visits or accompanying visitor programmes; it is uncommon in a general marketing department.
Verified destination material and an agreed itinerary are available.
The design excludes automated live safety advice and continuous visitor or employee tracking.
Build estimates cover preparation and reporting, with consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether tourist guiding actually falls within this role.
Visit frequency, destinations, language mix and group sizes.
Required guide qualifications and operational escalation limits.
Necessary visitor data, retention periods and access arrangements.
research_questions: Does reviewing a generated guide pack take less time than adapting existing approved notes?
Which visitor requirements must be confirmed directly rather than collected through a standard form?
new_work: Verify multilingual notes and refresh destination facts.
Maintain itinerary templates and escalation contacts.
Handle incomplete visitor briefs and scheduling exceptions.
Remove visitor information when its retention period ends.
